metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the short term (1-3 days) after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is neutral or flat.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward moves, leading to overconfidence in continuation; correct by reducing forecast slope after peak.
- When sentiment is absent or zero, model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias, forcing prices back toward historical mean too aggressively.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model tends to over-predict downward trends after recent highs, especially in 30-day horizon.
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum after a low, model fails to capture it — adjust forecast upward by 5-10% of recent 7-day average if sentiment is neutral.
- When true outcome deviates sharply from forecast, especially in 30-day horizon, check if recent sentiment was suppressed — if so, model may be under-reacting; increase forecast by 3-5% for next 7 days.
- If model forecast is consistently higher than true outcome in 30-day horizon, reduce forecast by 2-5% for next 14 days if sentiment remains flat or negative.
- If sentiment is zero and true outcome shows strong volatility, model tends to smooth out extremes — apply a 10% volatility buffer to forecast for next 7 days.
